```{r}
#| label: installation-docker
#| results: asis
#| echo: false

# `cf` holds a literal code-fence so no *source* line here is a bare ``` ---
# a bare fence line would be picked up by knitr's chunk partitioner as the
# chunk close and truncate this R code mid-string.
cf <- "```"
glue(
  "
  [![ghcr-latest] ![ghcr-size]](https://github.com/{org_nm}/{pkg_nm}/pkgs/container/{pkg_nm})

  [ghcr-latest]: <https://ghcr-badge.egpl.dev/{org_nm}/{pkg_nm}/latest_tag?color=%2344cc11&ignore=latest&label=docker-version-latest&trim=> \"GHCR latest tag\"
  [ghcr-size]: <https://ghcr-badge.egpl.dev/{org_nm}/{pkg_nm}/size?tag={ver}> \"GHCR image size\"

  The Docker image is available from the GitHub Container Registry at
  <https://github.com/{org_nm}/{pkg_nm}/pkgs/container/{pkg_nm}>.

  {cf}bash
  docker pull --platform linux/amd64 ghcr.io/{org_nm}/{pkg_nm}:{ver}
  {cf}

  ## Docker Compose

  The repo ships a `docker-compose.yaml` that wraps the CLI: it mounts a local
  input directory (`./in`, read-only) and output directory (`./out`), then
  tidies the input to parquet. Place a pipeline output directory under `./in`
  and run:

  {cf}bash
  mkdir -p in out
  docker compose run --rm {pkg_nm}
  {cf}

  Override defaults with environment variables (or a `.env` file):
  `IMAGE_TAG` (image tag, defaults to the pinned package version), `IN_DIR`,
  `OUT_DIR`, and `FORMAT` (`parquet` | `tsv` | `csv` | `rds`). The image's
  `ENTRYPOINT` is `{pkg_nm}.R`, so any flags after the service name append to
  it:

  {cf}bash
  IN_DIR=/path/to/samples docker compose run --rm {pkg_nm} tidy -d /data/in -o /data/out -f tsv
  {cf}
  "
)
```
